text: [Music]
Hello everyone and welcome to another
video. My track guide for the MX5 going
around summit point the Jefferson
layout. Let's get into it. Turn one is a
place where people will try and overtake
you in the race. So keep that in mind
when racing. But when qualifying, stay
on the left side of the track and I
break once I get to this tree here on
the right. I aim for about 90% brake
pressure, trailing that off all the way
to the curb. Once I get to the curb, I
want to let the car roll a little bit
before getting on the throttle just as
we exit. My goal is to come out just
about mid track so we have a little bit
more space for turn two. For the first
part of turn two, we want to cut the
inside curb. Once to go onto that curb,
I lift a little bit off the throttle. We
want to do the same thing for the second
part of turn two. And we want to end up
just about mid track for turn three.
There's no clear braking marker for turn
three, but this is just about where I
start to break. And I aim for about 80%
brake pressure. And I'm turning that off
till where the inside curb changes
color. This is also the point where we
want to start to accelerate again. We
want to ease in the throttle to make
sure we don't spin the car. I aim to
come out just about mid track for turn
three. That will make us drive fewer
meters and we will be able to cut in on
the curb for turn four. The car really
wants to go sideways here, so be careful
when racing. I don't recommend to try
and overtake into turn five, but some
people might try and do. But when
qualifying, stay on the right side of
the track. My braking marker is the last
three here on the left. When I lose
that, I go to about 65% brake pressure,
and I'm trailing that off all the way to
the inside curb. I prefer not to hit the
curb that much as I feel that that
unsettles the car quite a lot. If you
apex too early here, you will under
steer out to the grass, so make sure not
to apex too early. Once I get to the
inside curb, I start to apply the
throttle again. If we apex in the right
position and still go onto the grass,
you have gone onto the throttle too
early. Use all the room you need. Just
make sure you don't go onto the grass
that will spin the car. Turn six and
seven is a place where people will try
and overtake you in the race. But when
qualifying, you want to be as far right
as possible. I cut that last curb and I
also use it as my breaking point because
when the car land and it is stable, I
start to break. I start by going to
about 60% brake pressure. And then we
want to get close to the inside curb of
turn six. We're pretty much bleeding off
the brake onto the top of the little
hill. I prefer to take a tighter line
here. So, I go close to the inside curb
of turn six and out to just about mid
track before turning into turn seven.
And as we get to the top of the little
hill, we want to start to accelerate
again. Getting as close as we can to the
inside curb of turn 7, letting the car
walk out to the right side of the track,
even using the pit entry just to
maximize our exit speed. And that's my
lap in the MX5 around summit point, the
Jefferson layout of a time of 53
seconds.3. I have more track guides for
